clue.text: Fabulous creature in tin animal shelter

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
Noah's ark sheltered the animals from the Flood

explanation.surface: A mythical beast is found living inside a tin box that serves as a pet's shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's poem The Hunting of the Snark describes an imaginary beast, so it is a creature of fable.

clue.text: Well-rounded, clear-headed old man

indicators.note: clear-headed is read as the word clear giving only its head, its opening letter

parts.note: old man is slang for a husband, as is hubby

explanation.surface: A plump old fellow who nonetheless thinks lucidly.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump people are round in shape, so well-rounded here means fat rather than accomplished.

clue.text: Destined to be inducted as a priest

explanation.surface: A man is fated to take holy orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordained can mean fated or decreed by providence, and also formally admitted to the priesthood.

clue.text: Woman returns after riotous party in Italy

indicators.note: after places the reversed name behind the party word

parts.note: a rave is a wild party

indicators.note: returns tells us the woman's name is read backwards

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman goes back home following a wild party in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns ANN into NNA, which 'after' sets behind RAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravenna is a city in northern Italy famed for its mosaics, so it is a place found in that country.

clue.text: Call Mary odd — fit of tears!

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters of the words call Mary are put into a strange order

explanation.surface: Mary is being called strange and bursts into a bout of crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' shuffles CALLMARY; 'fit' only joins the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrymal is an adjective meaning relating to weeping or the glands producing them.

clue.text: Rhymester who has sampled Edgar Allan's work

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was the American writer
a taster is one who samples food or drink

explanation.surface: A minor poet who has dipped into the writings of Poe.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetaster is an inferior writer of verse, a mere versifier or rhymester.

clue.text: Make stable fellow a TV co-ordinator

parts.note: to anchor something is to fix it firmly
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A steady chap makes a good television co-ordinator.
explanation.definitionFit: A news presenter who links the reports and reporters of a broadcast co-ordinates the programme.

clue.text: Tycoon ensures veto's in force

parts.note: a bar is a ban or veto
on means operating or in effect

explanation.surface: A business magnate makes sure his prohibition is enforced.
explanation.definitionFit: A powerful businessman is called a baron, as in press baron or oil baron.

clue.text: Records left by pre-Christian soldiers

parts.note: AC is ante Christum, Latin for before Christ
TA is the Territorial Army, British reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: Documents bequeathed by soldiers of the era before Christ.
explanation.definitionFit: Acta are official proceedings or minutes, a set of written records.

clue.text: Tease blockhead in prison just as a game

indicators.note: in places the teasing and the head inside the prison

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement
to rib is to tease
the head of the word block is its first letter, B

explanation.surface: Mocking a dimwit in jail is treated as mere sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blockhead' looks like an insult but gives the head of 'block', B; 'in' puts RIBB inside CAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cribbage is a card game scored by pegging on a board.

clue.text: Dirty dog dined courtesy of minister?

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel or a contemptible person
ate means dined

explanation.surface: A scruffy dog has been fed thanks to a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant parish priest in the Church of England is a type of clergyman, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Colour comes out of fancy antimacassar

indicators.note: comes out of says the letters emerge from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A shade of colour emerges from an elaborate chair cover.
explanation.walkthrough: An antimacassar is a cloth placed over a chair back to protect it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyan is a greenish-blue shade, one of the printer's primary hues.

clue.text: Accident just avoided by neighbouring spinster

parts.note: near means close by or neighbouring
Miss is the title of an unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A crash was narrowly escaped thanks to the unmarried woman next door.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape from a collision is called this, the thing almost happening.

clue.text: Broke down when given lavish praise

explanation.surface: Someone collapsed emotionally on receiving fulsome compliments.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracked up means collapsed under strain, and also extolled, as in not all it is cracked up to be.

clue.text: Told to incorporate legendary bird in fabric

indicators.note: to incorporate means one word takes in the other

parts.note: bade is a past tense of bid, meaning told or ordered
the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend

explanation.surface: Someone was instructed to weave a mythical bird into a textile.
explanation.definitionFit: Brocade is a rich woven textile with a raised pattern.

clue.text: Promptly acquired two axes

indicators.note: two calls for the word for axes to be written twice

parts.note: to axe something is to chop it

explanation.surface: Someone quickly picked up a pair of hatchets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axes' is read as a verb, chops, not as tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Chop-chop is a pidgin-derived exclamation urging speed, meaning quickly.

clue.text: Insinuated that troublemaker falsified the facts

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous troublemaker
lied means told untruths

explanation.surface: Someone hinted that a mischief-maker had distorted the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: To insinuate is to suggest indirectly, which is what implied means.

clue.text: Apply cosmetics to flirt

parts.note: to make up is to put on cosmetics

explanation.surface: Putting on make-up in order to flirt.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up to someone is to court their favour or make amorous advances.

clue.text: Many stampeded and got trampled

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
rushed means charged headlong

explanation.surface: A crowd stampeded and people were trodden underfoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trodden on heavily is squashed flat.

clue.text: Chinese sheltered in rather large yacht

indicators.note: sheltered in means kept inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: sooner means rather, as in I would sooner stay

explanation.surface: A Chinese person took refuge in a fairly big sailing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a sailing vessel with two or more masts, a substantial yacht.

clue.text: How many see a knight in ecstasy?

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A question about how many people witness a knight in raptures.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a number, so it replies to a question of quantity.

clue.text: Vegetable Kate and Len eat for starters

indicators.note: for starters indicates the opening letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Kate and Len consume a green vegetable as a first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Kale is a leafy green of the cabbage family.

clue.text: Tell stories about a divine little boy

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the others

parts.note: to tell stories is to lie
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a divine being a clergyman

explanation.surface: Someone spins tales about a holy small child.
explanation.walkthrough: A divine is a theologian, hence DD (Doctor of Divinity); 'about' puts LIE round ADD.
explanation.definitionFit: Laddie is a Scottish diminutive for a young lad.

clue.text: Kick hothead under the stall

indicators.note: in a down clue under means the second piece comes below the first

parts.note: to boot is to kick
the head of the word hot is its first letter, H

explanation.surface: Someone kicks an angry young man beneath a market stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hothead' looks like a rash person, but it gives the head of 'hot'.
explanation.definitionFit: A booth is a small stall at a fair or market.

clue.text: Senior officer in Aden converted by a cleric

indicators.note: in places the officer within the rearranged letters
converted suggests the letters of Aden are changed into a new form

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: A commanding officer in Aden was converted to faith by a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' turns ADEN into DEAN, and 'in' places CO inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A deacon is an ordained minister ranking below a priest.

clue.text: Gramophone component needs solid case

parts.note: sound means solid or in good condition
a box is a case or container

explanation.surface: Part of a record player requires a sturdy casing.
explanation.definitionFit: On an old gramophone, the soundbox held the needle and diaphragm that made the record audible.

clue.text: Bet no sheep reappeared

indicators.note: reappeared signals the words no and sheep emerge backwards

parts.note: a tup is a ram

explanation.surface: A gambler wagers that no sheep turned up again.
explanation.definitionFit: To put money on a horse is to wager it, so the phrase means staked.

clue.text: Cattery in trouble? No doubt about it!

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters of cattery plus in are thrown into disarray

explanation.surface: Has the cats' boarding kennel run into difficulties? Definitely!
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute sureness is the state of having no doubt.
